questions.question: Dr. Marwani wishes to buy a professional premises for his practice. Dr. Soulami advises him to study the tax implications. According to the GTC, is the purchase of professional premises deductible from the taxable result?
options: Yes, fully deductible in the year of purchase
No, but the depreciation of the building is deductible
No, real estate purchase is never deductible
questions.explanation: Dr. Soulami explains: 'The purchase of professional premises is not deductible, but the depreciation of the building and interest on loans are deductible.' Dr. Marwani: 'I will optimize the depreciation.'

questions.question: Dr. Soulami has an LLC with a profit of 1,500,000 DH. Dr. Marwani helps him calculate the CIT. According to the 2026 scale, what is the amount of CIT due?
questions.explanation: Dr. Marwani explains: 'CIT is calculated by brackets: 300,000 × 10% = 30,000 DH, 700,000 × 20% = 140,000 DH, 500,000 × 35% = 175,000 DH. Total = 345,000 DH.' Dr. Soulami: 'I will plan for this amount.'

questions.question: Dr. Marwani, a natural person, has a turnover of 1,000,000 DH and a profit of 200,000 DH. Dr. Soulami helps him calculate his PIT. What is the tax due if the CM is 60,000 DH?
options: The higher amount between PIT and CM
questions.explanation: Dr. Soulami explains: 'The taxpayer pays the higher amount between PIT and CM. If CM is higher than PIT, they will pay the CM.' Dr. Marwani: 'I need to optimize my profit.'

questions.question: Dr. Soulami has an LLC with a profit of 400,000 DH. Dr. Marwani advises him to distribute dividends. According to the 2026 Finance Law, what is the withholding tax rate on dividends?
questions.explanation: Dr. Marwani explains: 'The withholding tax on dividends in 2026 is 11.25%, gradually decreasing towards 10% in 2027.' Dr. Soulami: 'I will anticipate this distribution.'

questions.question: Dr. Marwani wishes to buy a vehicle for his practice. Dr. Soulami reminds him of the deductibility rules. According to the GTC, is a utility vehicle 100% deductible?
options: No, the deduction is limited for all vehicles
No, personal vehicles are not deductible
questions.explanation: Dr. Soulami explains: 'Utility vehicles are 100% deductible. Passenger vehicles have a limited deduction.' Dr. Marwani: 'I will choose a utility vehicle.'

questions.question: Dr. Soulami, a natural person, has a taxable profit of 180,000 DH. Dr. Marwani reminds him of the deductions for family dependents. He has 2 dependent children. What is the amount of the reduction for family dependents?
questions.explanation: Dr. Marwani explains: 'The annual reduction is 600 DH per dependent, i.e. 1,200 DH for 2 children.' Dr. Soulami: 'I will apply this reduction.'

questions.question: Dr. Marwani has an LLC with a turnover of 3,000,000 DH. Dr. Soulami helps him calculate the CM. According to the 2026 Finance Law, what is the amount of CM due?
questions.explanation: Dr. Soulami explains: 'CM is 0.25% of turnover, i.e. 7,500 DH for 3,000,000 DH of turnover.' Dr. Marwani: 'This is a reasonable amount.'

questions.question: Dr. Soulami, a natural person, has a turnover of 450,000 DH. Dr. Marwani asks him to choose between RNS and RNR. According to the GTC, what is the main advantage of RNS?
questions.explanation: Dr. Marwani explains: 'RNS offers simplified accounting, but expenses are flat-rate.' Dr. Soulami: 'I will compare the two regimes.'

questions.question: Dr. Marwani has an LLC with a profit of 150,000 DH. Dr. Soulami helps him calculate the CIT. According to the 2026 scale, what is the amount of CIT due?
questions.explanation: Dr. Soulami explains: 'For the 0-300,000 DH bracket, the rate is 10%. The CIT due is 150,000 × 10% = 15,000 DH.' Dr. Marwani: 'This is very interesting.'

questions.question: Dr. Soulami, a natural person, has a tax deficit of 30,000 DH. Dr. Marwani reminds him of the carry-forward rules. Under RNS, is the deficit carry-forward allowed?
options: Yes, against profits of the following 4 years
No, RNS does not allow deficit carry-forward
Yes, against profits of the following 2 years
Yes, only against the following year
questions.explanation: Dr. Marwani explains: 'Under RNS, the deficit can be carried forward against profits of the following 4 years.' Dr. Soulami: 'I will track this carry-forward.'

questions.question: Dr. Marwani wishes to hire an assistant. Dr. Soulami reminds him of social security contributions. According to Moroccan legislation, what are the mandatory social security contributions for the employer?
questions.explanation: Dr. Soulami explains: 'The employer must contribute to CNSS (social insurance) and AMO (compulsory health insurance).' Dr. Marwani: 'I will plan for these charges.'

questions.question: Dr. Soulami has an LLC with a profit of 750,000 DH. Dr. Marwani helps him calculate the CIT. According to the 2026 scale, what is the amount of CIT due?
questions.explanation: Dr. Marwani explains: 'CIT is calculated by brackets: 300,000 × 10% = 30,000 DH, 450,000 × 20% = 90,000 DH. Total = 120,000 DH.' Dr. Soulami: 'Thank you for this calculation.'

questions.question: Dr. Marwani, a natural person, has a turnover of 2,000,000 DH. Dr. Soulami advises him to create an LLC. What is the main tax advantage of the LLC?
options: CIT rate of 10% to 20% vs progressive PIT up to 37%
questions.explanation: Dr. Soulami explains: 'The LLC allows a CIT rate of 10% to 20% vs progressive PIT up to 37%, a significant saving.' Dr. Marwani: 'I will create my LLC.'

questions.question: Dr. Soulami has an LLC with a turnover of 500,000 DH. Dr. Marwani helps him calculate the CM. According to the 2026 Finance Law, what is the amount of CM due?
questions.explanation: Dr. Marwani explains: 'CM is 0.25% of turnover, i.e. 1,250 DH. The floor being 3,000 DH, this amount is due.' Dr. Soulami: 'I will plan for 3,000 DH.'

questions.question: Dr. Marwani wishes to invest in management software. Dr. Soulami reminds him of the depreciation rules. According to the GTC, is software depreciable?
options: No, it is an immediate expense
Yes, over a period of 3 to 5 years
Yes, over a period of 10 years
No, software is non-depreciable intangible assets
questions.explanation: Dr. Soulami explains: 'Software is an intangible asset depreciable over 3 to 5 years depending on its useful life.' Dr. Marwani: 'I will depreciate this software.'

questions.question: Dr. Soulami, a natural person, has a taxable net income of 200,000 DH. Dr. Marwani helps him calculate his PIT. According to the 2026 scale, what is the amount of PIT due?
questions.explanation: Dr. Marwani explains: 'The progressive scale applies: 0-30,000 DH = 0%, 30,001-50,000 DH = 10% (2,000 DH), 50,001-60,000 DH = 20% (2,000 DH), 60,001-180,000 DH = 34% (40,800 DH), 180,001-200,000 DH = 37% (7,400 DH). Total = 52,200 DH.' Dr. Soulami: 'This is a significant amount.'

questions.question: Dr. Marwani has an LLC with a profit of 300,000 DH. Dr. Soulami helps him calculate the CIT. According to the 2026 scale, what is the amount of CIT due?
questions.explanation: Dr. Soulami explains: 'For the 0-300,000 DH bracket, the rate is 10%. The CIT due is 300,000 × 10% = 30,000 DH.' Dr. Marwani: 'This is very advantageous.'

questions.question: Dr. Soulami, a natural person, has a turnover of 700,000 DH. Dr. Marwani asks him to check his tax regime. Which regime is he automatically subject to?
questions.explanation: Dr. Marwani explains: 'RNR is the default regime for liberal professions whose annual turnover exceeds 500,000 DH.' Dr. Soulami: 'I am indeed under RNR.'

questions.question: Dr. Marwani wishes to buy dental consumables. Dr. Soulami reminds him of the deductibility rules. According to the GTC, are consumables deductible?
options: Yes, fully deductible in the year of purchase
questions.explanation: Dr. Soulami explains: 'Dental consumables are deductible expenses in the year of purchase.' Dr. Marwani: 'I will account for them properly.'

questions.question: Dr. Soulami has an LLC with a turnover of 1,000,000 DH and a taxable result of 0 DH. Dr. Marwani helps him calculate the CM. What is the amount of CM due?
questions.explanation: Dr. Marwani explains: 'CM is 0.25% of turnover, i.e. 2,500 DH. The floor being 3,000 DH, this amount is due, even in case of zero result.' Dr. Soulami: 'I still have to pay 3,000 DH.'

questions.question: Dr. Marwani, a natural person, has a turnover of 800,000 DH and a profit of 400,000 DH. Dr. Soulami helps him calculate the CM. What is the amount of CM due?
questions.explanation: Dr. Soulami explains: 'CM for natural persons is 6% of turnover, i.e. 800,000 × 6% = 48,000 DH.' Dr. Marwani: 'This is a significant amount.'

questions.question: Dr. Soulami has an LLC with a profit of 1,000,000 DH. Dr. Marwani helps him calculate the CIT. According to the 2026 scale, what is the amount of CIT due?
questions.explanation: Dr. Marwani explains: 'CIT is calculated by brackets: 300,000 × 10% = 30,000 DH, 700,000 × 20% = 140,000 DH. Total = 170,000 DH.' Dr. Soulami: 'I will plan for this amount.'

questions.question: Dr. Marwani wishes to associate with a colleague. Dr. Soulami advises him to choose the legal form. According to the GTC, which legal form is most suitable for an association of dentists?
questions.explanation: Dr. Soulami explains: 'SELARL (Liberal Practice Limited Liability Company) is specifically designed for liberal professions.' Dr. Marwani: 'I will create a SELARL.'

questions.question: Dr. Soulami, a natural person, has a turnover of 1,500,000 DH. Dr. Marwani advises him to optimize his structure. What is the main disadvantage of being a natural person for a high turnover?
questions.explanation: Dr. Marwani explains: 'The main disadvantage of being a natural person is the progressive PIT rate which can reach 37%, compared to 10% to 20% for CIT.' Dr. Soulami: 'I will create a company.'

questions.question: Dr. Marwani, after optimizing his tax management with Dr. Soulami, receives his congratulations. What is the next step for Dr. Marwani?
options: Become an expert in tax management for dental practices
questions.explanation: Dr. Soulami explains: 'Mastery of tax management is a valuable skill. Becoming an expert is the next step.' Dr. Marwani: 'I will train in advanced taxation.'
